service.description:
Events (WorkEffort, WetEvent by default) for a calendar grid such as the FullCalendar JS library (http://fullcalendar.io/) in a range of days (start and end, yyyy-MM-dd in the user's time zone, or time stamps taken as their days). An event is in when it overlaps the range and is: - in a calendar of calendarIdList the user may see (mantle.work.CalendarServices.check#CalendarAccess; one the user may not see is left out and named in skippedCalendarIdList; one with free/busy permission only shows its events as Busy, without their details), or - one where a party of partyId or partyIdList is a current WorkEffortParty or the owner (with calendarIdList and no party given, the current user's party: the user's calendars plus every event the user is on), or - one that books a facility of facilityId or facilityIdList (WorkEffortFacility not denied, or the event's own WorkEffort.facilityId) or an asset of assetId or assetIdList (WorkEffortAssetAssign not denied and not cancelled before the event), or - visible to all users (WevAllUsers) when parties or calendars are asked for and includeAllUsers is true. An event the asked parties declined (every current row of theirs WeptDeclined or WeptUnassigned, and none of them the owner) is left out unless showDeclined or it is in an asked calendar or booked resource; an invitation the user declined (the user's own rows so, and the user not its owner) is left out unless showDeclined even when it is in an asked calendar, though not when it books an asked resource. With publishToken (a publish link, mantle.work.CalendarServices.share#Calendar) only that calendar's events, at the link's permission, and publishPassword must match its password. With rootWorkEffortId (a project; IronStone Projects' calendar, design-projects.md §15 Calendar project filter) only the events linked to it (WorkEffortRecord of mantle.work.effort.WorkEffort) are in: all of them for a user who is a current party of the project (or ADMIN), else those the user owns or is a party of; the project's milestones, releases, sprints and work items are the caller's to read.
A recurring event is expanded by get#EventInstances: an RFC 5545 rule (WorkEffortRecurrence) through the framework's ICalendar tool, without which only the series' own first instance shows; an instance changed on its own (WorkEffortAssoc WeatRecurrenceInstance) replaces the generated one; the older recurStartCron with recurLimit (the number of instances) and recurEndDate.
An event: id (the work effort, a recurring event's for each instance), title (titleGString, Busy for free/busy), start and end (yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss in the user's time zone, or for an all-day event yyyy-MM-dd with end the day after the last day, as FullCalendar and iCalendar take it; end null when the event has none), allDay, url (with urlGString), workEffortId, workEffortTypeEnumId, statusId, calendarId and color (of the first asked calendar it is in), partyStatusId and availabilityEnumId (the user's, else the first asked party's WorkEffortParty), bookingStatusId (of an asked facility or asset), recurring, recurringEventId (the series), instanceStart (the start of the instance it is, for a recurring event), startMillis and endMillis, freeBusyOnly, location, ownerPartyId and ownerName (the organizer; none of the three for a free/busy event).

parameter.name: workEffortTypeEnumIds
parameter.description: Default WetEvent

parameter.name: rootWorkEffortId
parameter.description: A project: only its linked events (WorkEffortRecord)

parameter.name: url
parameter.description: Only returned if urlGString is specified

service.description:
The instances of work efforts (events, maps of their WorkEffort fields) that overlap a range, each {workEffortId, start and end (epoch millis; end null when the event has none), allDay, startDay and endDay (an all-day instance's first day and the day after its last, yyyy-MM-dd in the user's time zone), recurring, seriesWorkEffortId and recurrenceStart (a recurring instance's series and the start the rule gives it), workEffort (its fields)}, in order of start.
- A work effort with a WorkEffortRecurrence is a series: its rule is expanded by the framework's ICalendar tool, ec.factory.getTool('ICalendar').expand(rrule, dtstart, timeZone, exdates, rdates, rangeStart, rangeEnd), with rrule the RRULE value, dtstart the series' first start (epoch millis; for an all-day series the start of its first day in timeZone), timeZone the recurrence's (else the user's) IANA name, exdates and rdates the lists of the EXDATE and RDATE values as stored (RFC 5545 DATE-TIME or DATE text), and rangeStart and rangeEnd epoch millis; it returns the instance starts (epoch millis, ascending, dtstart among them as RFC 5545 counts it) from rangeStart to rangeEnd, the rule's COUNT and UNTIL applied, the EXDATEs left out and the RDATEs added. Without the tool only the series' first instance is returned (logged once). - An instance changed on its own is a WorkEffort linked from the series by WorkEffortAssoc WeatRecurrenceInstance whose fromDate is the start of the instance it replaces: the generated instance gives way to it, and it is returned with its own dates (a cancelled one, WeCancelled, removes the instance). - The older recurStartCron: the cron's fire times after the start's day, at most recurLimit of them and none after recurEndDate, each as long as the first instance. - Anything else is its one instance.

parameter.name: toolMissing
parameter.description: A series was not expanded for want of the tool

parameter.name: calendarId
parameter.description: A calendar to put the event in (mantle.work.CalendarServices.add#CalendarEvent: edit permission on it)

parameter.name: rrule
parameter.description: The RFC 5545 RRULE of a recurring event (store#EventRecurrence)

service.description: What the current user may do with an event (or another work effort): edit as its organizer (the owner, WorkEffort.ownerPartyId, is the user's party) or with edit permission on a calendar it is in (not a subscription calendar, whose events come from the feed); view as well as an attendee (a current WorkEffortParty), with view permission on a calendar it is in, or when it is visible to all users (WevAllUsers). With permission view or edit, an error when the user may not; an event the user may not view is "not found".

parameter.name: permission
parameter.description: view or edit

service.description: The iCalendar event maps of work efforts (see the comment at the top of mantle.work.CalendarServices), for the ICalendar tool's write: the series with their rules, plus the instances of those series changed on their own (with recurrenceId), the organizer and the attendees with their answers, and the current user's reminders as alarms. An attendee's role is OPT-PARTICIPANT when the party's expectation is WepeInvRequested (optional), NON-PARTICIPANT for WepeFyi, else REQ-PARTICIPANT.

Sets the recurrence of an event (edit access): rrule is the RFC 5545 RRULE value (FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO), exdates and rdates comma separated EXDATE and RDATE values, timeZone an IANA name (default the user's). An empty rrule and rdates make it a single event again.

Changes an event's time (a move or resize on a calendar grid, or the When of an event screen) and optionally its name, location and description, with edit access (check#EventAccess: the organizer or an editor of a calendar it is in). start and end are yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm in the user's time zone, or days for an all-day event (end the last day); allDay Y or N changes the kind. A recurring event (WorkEffortRecurrence) changes by scope, for the instance that starts at instanceStart (its start as the rule gives it, yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm or a day; the series' first without it): - this: that instance alone, as an instance WorkEffort linked from the series (WorkEffortAssoc WeatRecurrenceInstance, fromDate the rule's start) with the series' people, calendars, rooms and equipment; an instance already changed (its own workEffortId, or the series' with its instanceStart) is changed; - following: the series ends before the instance (UNTIL, its COUNT counted down into the new series) and a new series with the same rule, people, calendars, rooms, equipment and reminders starts at the new time, taking the instances changed after it (the first instance's following is all); - all (the default): the series moves by the instance's change (BYDAY and BYMONTHDAY follow a change of day), its changed instances keyed again; with no new time the series' own fields change. A change of time checks the bookings of the event it lands on (check#ResourceBookings): a clash with another booking refuses the change unless allowConflicts, and a booking of a resource with approvers is requested again. With notify Y the attendees are told (send#EventInvitations, to the changed ones, of the event changed and, when the series was split, of the series that ended to those outside only; one that fails is logged). targetWorkEffortId is the work effort the change landed on, seriesWorkEffortId its series (null for a single event).

parameter.name: scope
parameter.description: this, following or all

parameter.name: allDay
parameter.description: Y or N; empty keeps the kind

parameter.name: notify
parameter.description: Y to tell the attendees

parameter.name: eventUrl
parameter.description: The event's screen, for the notifications' link

service.description: Cancels an event (WeCancelled), with edit access (check#EventAccess); a recurring event by scope as update#EventOccurrence, for the instance that starts at instanceStart: - this: the instance only, an EXDATE of the series' rule (an instance changed on its own is cancelled as well); - following: the series ends before it (UNTIL), and the instances changed after it are cancelled (the first instance's following is all); - all (the default): the series and its changed instances. With notify Y the attendees are told (send#EventInvitations to every attendee of the series, or of the event: a cancel when it is cancelled, the update otherwise; one that fails is logged). cancelledWorkEffortIds are the work efforts cancelled; exdate is the EXDATE added, for this.

parameter.name: scope
parameter.description: this, following or all

parameter.name: notify
parameter.description: Y to tell the attendees

parameter.name: eventUrl
parameter.description: The event's screen, for the notifications' link

service.description: The current user's answer to an event invitation, on the user's own current WorkEffortParty rows of the event: accept (WeptAssigned), tentative (WeptTentative) or decline (WeptDeclined), with an optional message (the row's comments). The organizer (the event's owner) gets a notification on the topic EventInvitationResponse when the organizer is another user; an organizer outside (no user, an email address) gets an iMIP REPLY written by the framework's ICalendar tool, which carries the replying attendee only (RFC 5546). A failed notification is logged; the answer stays.

parameter.name: response
parameter.description: accept, tentative or decline

parameter.name: eventUrl
parameter.description: The event's screen, for the notification's link

parameter.name: replyIcsText
parameter.description: The iMIP REPLY sent to an organizer outside, else null

service.description: What an event's invitation tells, as a digest (8 hex digits of a hash of its name, time, place, meeting rooms, recurrence and whether it is cancelled): send#EventInvitations keeps it on each attendee's WorkEffortParty (invitationDigest, with invitationSentDate) when it sends one, and a changed event has another digest. Per attendee (the current WorkEffortParty parties but the organizer and the current user, as send#EventInvitations sends) whether that attendee has the latest invitation: upToDate when one was sent and its digest is the event's now; pendingPartyIdList are the others (none sent, or the event changed since). roomIdList are the meeting rooms in the digest. View access to the event (check#EventAccess) unless authorization is disabled.

parameter.name: attendee
parameter.description: partyId, invitationSentDate, invitationDigest, sentBefore, upToDate

service.description:
Sends the invitations of an event (edit access) to its new or changed attendees only: the current WorkEffortParty parties other than the organizer and the current user whose last invitation (invitationSentDate) is missing, or whose invitationDigest differs from the event's now (its name, time, place, rooms, recurrence and whether it is cancelled); partyIdList limits it to those parties, resendAll sends to every attendee. A party with a user account gets a notification on the topic EventInvitation (update true when it had one before); a party without one gets an email to its primary address (template MANTLE_CALENDAR_EMAIL, from the organizer's address), with the iMIP REQUEST (an .ics part) once the framework's ICalendar tool exists. Each attendee stands alone: one that fails is logged and named in skippedList, the rest are sent; a party with neither a user nor an email address is skipped. The digest is get#InvitationDigest's.
With attendeeRemoved the parties of partyIdList are being taken off the event (remove#EventAttendee, before it ends their rows): each that had an invitation gets its cancel, a notification with removed and cancelled true, or an email with the iMIP CANCEL that names that attendee only (RFC 5546 3.2.5); one that never had an invitation gets nothing, and their rows keep their digest.
With outsideOnly only the parties without a user account are sent to (by email, the iMIP their calendar programs read), and the rows of the users are brought up to date without a notification: for the series that ends where update#EventOccurrence splits one, whose users hear of the new series.

parameter.name: message
parameter.description: A note to the attendees

parameter.name: eventUrl
parameter.description: The event's screen, for the notification's link

parameter.name: skipped
parameter.description: partyId, reason

parameter.name: icsTextMap
parameter.description: The iMIP text emailed to each party without a user, by partyId

service.description: Takes a person off an event (edit access): the party's current WorkEffortParty rows end (thruDate now); the organizer stays. A party who had an invitation is told, unless notify is false: a user by a notification on EventInvitation (removed true), a party without a user by email with the iMIP CANCEL that names them as its attendee (send#EventInvitations with attendeeRemoved, before the rows end). A notice that fails is logged and the removal stands.

parameter.name: message
parameter.description: A note to the attendee

parameter.name: eventUrl
parameter.description: The event's screen, for the notification's link

parameter.name: notified
parameter.description: The attendee was sent the cancel

parameter.name: cancelIcsText
parameter.description: The iMIP CANCEL emailed to a party without a user

service.description: Busy times of parties, meeting rooms (facilities) and equipment (assets) from fromDate to thruDate (at most 92 days), for "Find a time" and booking, with no event details: - a party: the events (and WetTimeOff, status away) where it is a current WorkEffortParty and has not declined (an invitation not answered yet or answered tentative is tentative; a row with availability WeptaAvailable is not busy), and the events it owns; - a facility: its WorkEffortFacility bookings (requested while waiting for approval; denied ones are not busy) and the events whose WorkEffort.facilityId it is; - an asset: its WorkEffortAssetAssign bookings, as for a facility. Cancelled events are not busy, and excludeWorkEffortId (the event being scheduled) is left out. Recurring events count by get#EventInstances. A party's working hours (workingHourList) are its WetAvailable work efforts (usually recurring) when it has any, else with workingHoursOnly 09:00 to 17:00 Monday to Friday in the user's time zone. With durationMinutes, suggestedSlotList has up to suggestionLimit free slots of that length, starting every slotMinutes from now or fromDate, when no one is busy (tentative and requested count as busy) and, with workingHoursOnly, inside every party's working hours.

parameter.name: freeBusy
parameter.description: resourceType (party, facility or asset), partyId, facilityId or assetId, busyList [{fromDate, thruDate, status (busy, tentative, requested or away)}], workingHourList [{fromDate, thruDate}] (a party with working hours)

parameter.name: slot
parameter.description: fromDate, thruDate

service.description: Books a meeting room (facilityId: a WorkEffortFacility) or equipment (assetId: a WorkEffortAssetAssign) for an event, with edit access to the event, at the event's time. Without a booking policy the booking is assigned at once (WefAssigned, WeaaAssigned); a resource with a policy is requested (WefRequested, WeaaRequested) and waits for its approvers. The policy is a placeholder until Maintenance designs it: a resource needs approval when it has a current approver, a FacilityParty (a facility) or AssetPartyAssignment (an asset) of role BookingApprover, unless the user is one. A booking that overlaps another of the same resource (not denied, not cancelled) is refused, unless allowConflicts, which books it and returns the conflicts. A denied booking asked again is asked again; a current one is returned as it is.

parameter.name: conflict
parameter.description: workEffortId, workEffortName, fromDate, thruDate, bookingStatusId

service.description: Cancels the booking of a meeting room (deletes the WorkEffortFacility) or equipment (ends the current WorkEffortAssetAssign rows, thruDate now) of an event, with edit access to the event.

Checks the meeting room and equipment bookings of an event at its time now, as after a move (update#EventOccurrence calls it): each current booking (a WorkEffortFacility that is not denied, a WorkEffortAssetAssign that is not denied and not ended) against the other bookings of its resource, by the rule of book#Resource; the other events of the same recurring series do not clash. A clash refuses (an error naming the resource and the events it clashes with) unless allowConflicts, which keeps the booking and lists the clash in conflictList. By book#Resource's booking policy, with reapprove (the default) a booking that was assigned for a resource with approvers the user is not one of is requested again (WefRequested, WeaaRequested): the approval was for the old time. bookingList has each booking {facilityId or assetId, resourceName, statusId, previousStatusId, conflictList}. Edit access to the event.

parameter.name: conflict
parameter.description: facilityId or assetId, resourceName, workEffortId, workEffortName, fromDate, thruDate, bookingStatusId

service.description: Sets the current user's reminders of an event or a task (the editable rows of EventDetail): reminderList is the whole list, each {offsetMinutes (before the start of an event, the due date of a task; 0 to 43200), methodEnumId (WermNotification, the default, or WermEmail)}. A reminder already there with the same offset and method stays (with its sentDate), the others are removed. The user's party must be on the work effort (a current WorkEffortParty) or own it.

parameter.name: partyId
parameter.description: Default the user's party; only the user's own

service.description: The reminder job (every minute): each WorkEffortReminder that is due is sent to its party, each in a transaction of its own (send#WorkEffortReminder), and one that fails is logged and tried again on the next run. A reminder is due offsetMinutes before an instance of its event starts (a task's due date), once per instance (an instance whose reminder time is after the reminder's sentDate), while the instance has not ended (a task within a day of its due date); a snoozed reminder (snoozedThruDate) is held back until then and sent again then. Cancelled events and completed, closed or cancelled tasks get none.

Sends one reminder of an instance (send#DueReminders): a notification on the topic WorkEffortReminder to the party's users (WermNotification; a party with no user gets an email), or an email to the party's primary address (WermEmail; template MANTLE_CALENDAR_EMAIL, from the mantle.calendar.email.from property or the work effort owner's address). Sets sentDate and clears snoozedThruDate; a party that can be reached by neither is logged and not tried again.

parameter.name: method
parameter.description: notification, email or none

service.description: Holds back the current user's reminder of a work effort (reminderSeqId, else all of the user's reminders of it) until snoozedThruDate, by default snoozeMinutes (10) from now; the reminder job sends it again then.

Find the next business day skipping Saturday and Sunday unless specified not to, and skipping holidays by organizationPartyId (WorkEffort.ownerPartyId) and workEffortCategoryIds. WorkEffort records must have purposeEnumId=WepHoliday and the a single day date in the WorkEffort.allDayStart field.

parameter.name: organizationPartyId
parameter.description: If specified matches against WorkEffort.ownerPartId to find holidays

parameter.name: workEffortCategoryIds
parameter.description: If specified matches against WorkEffort records in these categories to find holidays, such as HolidayUsaBank or HolidayUsaFed

service.description: Looks into the future businessDays days, checking each day to see if it is a business day and if not it is skipped over; for example if starting on a Friday and Sat/Sun plus a holiday on Monday are skipped the following Tuesday will be the next business day, and if going forward 5 business days and there are no other holiday then it will move forward 3 more business days (4 so far) to the following Friday, then going to the next business day to get 5 it jumps to the following Monday, in this case we went forward 5 business days and skipped 5 days so calendarDays will be 10
